summary: merge-grid-stats postinstall runs SSRF probes and drops recon files outside its install directory
details: The package advertises itself as a lightweight utility for merge-style grid game scoring, but the shipped index.js only contains trivial score/localStorage helpers. All non-trivial behavior lives in a postinstall script (install-cb.js, declared in package.json.scripts.postinstall) that runs unconditionally on npm install. The postinstall issues HTTPS GET probes to a hardcoded external host, mtsrc-test.sankuai.com, with a unique marker path /ssrf?src=nocode-rce-v13, and also probes loopback services at 127.0.0.1:80 and 127.0.0.1:8080. TLS certificate verification is disabled (rejectUnauthorized: false). After probing, it writes NCODE_SSRF.txt (containing the installer's hostname and probe response bodies, including any internal-network responses) and NCODE_POC_MARKER.txt into the current working directory and into../ and../../, deliberately escaping the package's own install directory. Source comments self-label the behavior as a PoC. The mismatch between the advertised purpose and the install-time behavior, along with generic placeholder author metadata (merge-tools@example.com), matches the cover-story pattern for install-time supply-chain payloads.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
